## Overview

My research program uses demographic and statistical methods to understand how
population processes and geographic context shape human health and wellbeing.
Three commitments run through this work: substantive questions about health and
inequality, careful attention to spatial and multilevel structure in data, and a
methodological preference for models that are transparent and reproducible. Most
of my analysis is carried out in R, drawing on large survey and administrative
datasets from sources such as the U.S. Census, the Demographic and Health
Surveys, and vital statistics systems.

The full publication record is available on
[Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/citations?hl=en&user=ihmc__0AAAAJ),
and worked examples and course code are posted on
[RPubs](https://rpubs.com/corey_sparks) and
[GitHub](https://github.com/coreysparks).

## Research themes

::: {.research-area}
### Spatial demography and geographic inequality

I examine how mortality, poverty, and social outcomes cluster across places, using
exploratory spatial data analysis and spatial regression to study residential
segregation, poverty concentration, and local spatial dependence. This line of
work includes both substantive studies of segregation and methodological
contributions on measuring and modeling spatial structure in the social sciences.
:::

::: {.research-area}
### Population health and mortality

I study mortality, maternal and child health, substance use, and nutrition,
with attention to how contextual conditions and social position shape risk across
populations. Recent work includes analyses of drug overdose mortality across
US-born and immigrant groups and trends in maternal mortality in the United States.
:::

::: {.research-area}
### Statistical and predictive methods

I develop and apply hierarchical and Bayesian models, small-area estimation,
hierarchical forecasting, and machine learning to demographic and public health
problems, including undernutrition prediction and mortality forecasting for
resource allocation.
:::

::: {.research-area}
### Workforce and life-course demography

I also study life-course and cohort dynamics, including how the timing of labor
market entry shapes early-career trajectories, using longitudinal data to separate
structural drivers from period shocks.
:::
